narrative:
After a chilly start in valleys, sunshine and a warmer afternoon are the big stories today. Wednesday is even warmer, with highs near records for the date. Thursday stays warm; I cannot rule out a stray afternoon shower north, near the NC/VA border. The turn comes Friday: scattered afternoon showers with a cold front, then a sharply colder, windy night. The biggest tourism weekend of the year rolls out the welcome rug for Fall! Saturday is chilly and breezy, and Sunday morning brings the first widespread frost of the season.

Here's an analysis of all the Isaias rain data from our weather stations across Western NC and SW VA.

This week's Monday Message recaps Isaias rainfall, lays out the warm week ahead, followed by a much cooler (but dry) weekend upcoming.

Forecast Discussion

High pressure builds over us from the southwest today and Wednesday. Light wind and full sun push temperatures to near-record highs by Wednesday.

A front approaches Wednesday night and stalls to our north Thursday. We stay on its warm side. I cannot rule out a stray afternoon shower near the Virginia line, closer to the retreating front.

A stronger cold front crosses Friday afternoon from the west with scattered showers. The showers end quickly behind the front, and sharply colder air arrives Friday night on a gusty northwest wind.

Saturday is chilly and breezy. High pressure settles overhead Saturday night and Sunday, and the wind settles. That sets up our first widespread frost Sunday morning. Sunday stays cool under full sun.

Monday starts frosty in the valleys again, then temperatures recover modestly in the afternoon as the high drifts east. Dry weather holds into early next week.
